review_notes: I read the whole file and the State.lean simp setup (ket_apply is simp). I grepped LeanQuantumAlg for uses of the apply, ofPerm, mul_apply and conjTranspose lemmas. I have not run Lean, so the simp-priority claims come from reading the lemma statements, not from observed simplifier behaviour. The linear-algebra simp lemmas (applyVec_add, applyVec_smul and similar) are consistent and look fine. The compatibility aliases apply_add and its siblings are not simp lemmas, so they cause no competing-rule problem. The three findings are real but low-to-moderate severity.

findings.excerpt:
theorem ofPerm_apply (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 ^ n))) (ψ : PureState n)
    (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) : (ofPerm σ).apply ψ i = ψ (σ i) := by
findings.problem: `apply_apply` is `@[simp]` and rewrites every `G.apply ψ i` to a sum `∑ j, G i j * ψ j`. The canonical pointwise lemmas for the permutation gate, `ofPerm_apply` (`(ofPerm σ).apply ψ i = ψ (σ i)`) and `ofPerm_apply_ket`, are not simp. There is also no simp lemma giving the matrix entries of `ofPerm σ`; `ofPerm` is a plain `def` and no `coe_ofPerm` exists. So `simp` turns `(ofPerm σ).apply ψ i` into an opaque sum over `(ofPerm σ) i j`. The desired normal form `ψ (σ i)` is unreachable, and the same happens to `(ofPerm σ).apply (ket x)`. The downstream uses show the cost. SwapTest and Oracle use `rw [… ofPerm_apply …]` and `rw [xorOracle, ofPerm_apply_ket]` by hand. BellPair resorts to `simp +decide [… Gate.apply_apply, CNOT, Gate.ofPerm, Fin.sum_univ_four]`, which unfolds the permutation down to `permMatrix`.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `ofPerm_apply` and `ofPerm_apply_ket` with `@[simp]`. Also add a lemma such as `coe_ofPerm : ((ofPerm σ : Gate n) : HilbertOperator n) = σ.permMatrix ℂ := rfl`, so matrix-entry goals are not stuck either. Because `apply_apply` and `ofPerm_apply` both match `(ofPerm σ).apply ψ i`, give `ofPerm_apply` higher priority (e.g. `@[simp high]`) or make `apply_apply` non-simp. That way the pointwise permutation form wins deterministically over the generic sum expansion.
findings.benefit: Goals like `(swapRegisters n).apply (psi.tensor phi) i` or `(xorOracle f).apply ψ i` would simplify to the one-term form `ψ (σ i)` instead of an unwanted `permMatrix` sum. Proofs such as SwapTest and Oracle could use `simp` instead of manual `rw` chains.

findings.excerpt:
theorem mul_applyVec (A B : HilbertOperator n) (ψ : StateVector n) :
    applyVec (A * B) ψ = applyVec A (applyVec B ψ) := by
findings.problem: The action of operators and gates on vectors has a simp set for `+`, `-`, `•`, negation, `1` and operator addition and scalar action (`applyVec_add`, `applyVec_smul`, `add_applyVec`, `smul_applyVec`, `one_applyVec`, `Gate.one_apply`). The remaining generator, multiplication, has no simp lemma in any of its three forms: `HilbertOperator.mul_applyVec`, `Gate.mul_applyVec` and `Gate.mul_apply`. A term like `applyVec (A * B) ψ` or `(G * K).apply ψ` is therefore a simp-stuck normal form. Instead, because `applyVec_apply` and `apply_apply` are simp, a pointwise goal `(G * K).apply ψ i` is expanded to a sum over `(G * K) i j`. The simp set is not closed under composition even though `1` is covered.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `HilbertOperator.mul_applyVec`, `Gate.mul_applyVec` and `Gate.mul_apply` as `@[simp]`, oriented as they already are (product on the left, nested application on the right). The right-hand side is strictly smaller in multiplication depth, so this is terminating. `coe_mul` has a different head and does not conflict. The existing reverse rewrites `← Gate.mul_applyVec` use `rw`, so they are unaffected.
findings.benefit: Circuit-composition goals such as `(G * K).apply ψ` normalise to nested application, consistent with the other linearity lemmas. Users no longer need hand-written `rw [Gate.mul_applyVec, Gate.mul_applyVec, …]` chains, as in ControlledTransform and HadamardTest. Nor do they need the `pow_succ'` / `Gate.mul_apply` rewriting seen in AmplitudeAmplification.

findings.problem: The gate inverse is provided through `Inv (Gate n)` as `⟨conjTranspose⟩`, but the only simp lemma about it, `coe_conjTranspose`, is stated for `G.conjTranspose`. The notation `G⁻¹` is a different head symbol. Because `Inv.inv` is not unfolded by simp, `((G⁻¹ : Gate n) : HilbertOperator n)` is stuck and `coe_conjTranspose` never fires on it. There is also no lemma relating `G⁻¹` to `conjTranspose`, and no `inv_applyVec` or `inv_mul` facts. A user who writes `G⁻¹` (the natural notation for the `Inv` instance) gets no simp support. The two spellings of the same gate are separate normal forms.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem coe_inv (G : Gate n) : ((G⁻¹ : Gate n) : HilbertOperator n) = (G : HilbertOperator n).conjTranspose := rfl`. Optionally add `inv_def : G⁻¹ = G.conjTranspose := rfl` as a non-simp bridge. Alternatively, state `coe_conjTranspose` for `G⁻¹` and keep `conjTranspose` as the internal construction. Pick one canonical form so simp has a single normal form for the adjoint gate.
findings.benefit: Matrix-level goals involving `G⁻¹` reduce to `(G : HilbertOperator n)ᴴ` under `simp`. This removes the ambiguity between `G⁻¹` and `G.conjTranspose`.
